meta.topic: SLATE research: life gaps (restaurant reservations, television, hobby lessons and leagues, volunteering, acting prep, audition dress, child's day, household chores, police reports for lost documents, boating exam pass marks) in New York, Los Angeles, New Haven CT, London, Dublin, Toronto, Vancouver and Mexico City
meta.method: WebSearch to find each publisher; WebFetch, or curl with a browser user agent where WebFetch was refused, to read the publisher's own page. Public registration systems (ActiveNet estimate-price records for YMCA LA, City of Toronto and Vancouver Park Board; Resy's venue API behind resy.com) were read directly and count as the publisher's page. 'confirmed: true' means the figure was read on the publisher's own page (or a state body's page where noted) on 2026-10-03; 'confirmed: false' means it came from a search-engine summary or a third party, and the note says which. Nothing is invented or estimated; derived figures (such as session counts from date spans) are labelled in the note. Existing files were checked first: school hours, 2026-27 term dates and centre childcare prices are already in research-referrals-childday.json, and parkrun, running clubs and volunteering platforms are in research-clubs.json, so childDay here adds after-school programmes and fills gaps only. The hobby leagues are under hobbyLeagues.
meta.currencies: USD for US towns, GBP for London, EUR for Dublin, CAD for Toronto and Vancouver, MXN for Mexico City, unless an entry says otherwise.

television.item: Ofcom COSTA advertising limits on public service channels (ITV, STV, Channel 4, S4C, Channel 5)

figures.psbMaxBreakLength: 3 min 50 s, of which ads max 3 min 30 s

television.note: Ofcom's own COSTA PDF returns 403 (Cloudflare). The 7 and 8 min PSB averages were read on Wiggin LLP (law firm); Ofcom decided on 2023-09-28 not to relax them. The 12-min clock-hour cap and the break-length figures come from a search summary of the COSTA PDF (last updated 28 April 2022). No 2025-26 change was found. Non-PSB daily average: Marketing Week (2011) reported 9 min/hour.

Variety (Michael Schneider): 'a half-hour (actually, 21 minutes with commercials) or an hourlong (e.g., 44 minutes plus ads) time slot'. Cable comedies were held to a '21-minute limit'. Streaming hour-long episodes run 'a full hour… 15 minutes more than your average drama on an ad-supported broadcast or cable channel'. Gilded Age episodes ran 46-56 min; Book of Boba Fett 39-61 min. Trade press, not a regulator: these are industry conventions, not rules.
THR (Bryn Sandberg): 'once-sacrosanct runtime barriers, 42 minutes for dramas and 22 for comedies'. Netflix's Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt ran 23-36 min (one episode 21 min); Westworld averaged 61 min.
